text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two senior police officers are arrested over the recent murders of two Nyakinyua Investments Company officials.
- The late minister Zachary Onyonka receives a hero's send off at a burial marked by a heavy downpour.
- Three opposition party officials tell opposition FORD-Asili Chairman Kenneth Matiba to rejoin the ruling Kenya African National Union if he cannot agree with what the opposition is fighting for.
- A government vehicle carrying a cache of firearms is intercepted at a police checkpoint at Moyale near the Kenya-Ethiopian border.
- A Nigerian cargo plane crashlands on the main runway at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.
- The High Court dismisses with costs a bid by an international investment company seeking to stay a 19.5 million shillings decree made in favour of the collapsed Meridien Biao Bank.
- Lonhro East Africa Chairman Mark Too praises the overnment for increases in import duty on wheat, maize, rice, milk and sugar.
- The Kenya Shoe and Leather Workers Union lashes out at shippers opposing government efforts to curb the importation of sub-standard goods, saying it wanted to push Kenyans out of jobs.
